full_caption: Fitzwilliam Marchetti-Doyle, Appellant, v. Copperfield Row Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: This action turns on the construction of three riders appended to a commercial lease between Fitzwilliam Marchetti-Doyle, as landlord, and Copperfield Row Capital Servicing, LLC, as tenant, for 680 square feet at 3070 Ferndale Road, Grayrock, FH.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A late charge and default interest may be imposed cumulatively only where the lease says so expressly. Absent express language, imposing both amounts to a double recovery for the same delay.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: A rider is read as part of the integrated lease. Where a rider and the printed form conflict, the rider controls, because it represents the parties' specific and later-negotiated intent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The Estoppel Rider requires the tenant to deliver a certificate within 45 days of request. Failure to deliver operates as an admission of the facts stated in the landlord's proposed form only where the rider so provides.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Internet orders fulfilled from the leased premises fall within the definition of gross sales; orders merely placed at a kiosk on the premises and shipped from a remote warehouse do not.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The Late Fee Rider assesses a charge of 10 percent of any installment not received by the 15th day of the month, together with interest at 9 percent per annum on the unpaid balance from the due date.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The Percentage Rent Rider obligates Copperfield Row Capital Servicing, LLC to pay 4 percent of annual gross sales in excess of a breakpoint of $700,000, with 'gross sales' defined to exclude returns, sales taxes collected, and inter-store transfers.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The Holdover Rider fixes holdover rent at 1.25 times the last monthly installment. Such a provision is enforceable as liquidated damages where holdover harm is difficult to estimate and the multiplier is not grossly disproportionate.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The Continuous Operation Rider requires the tenant to remain open during the hours the shopping center is open. It is enforceable by injunction only where damages are inadequate; a going-dark clause with a stated liquidated remedy displaces injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The Assignment and Subletting Rider conditions transfer on the landlord's consent, 'which shall not be unreasonably withheld.' Reasonableness is measured by objective commercial criteria: the proposed transferee's financial capacity, use, and experience.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Judgment for Copperfield Row Capital Servicing, LLC on the late-fee and default-interest claim is affirmed; judgment for Fitzwilliam Marchetti-Doyle on the percentage-rent claim is affirmed as modified.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — LATE FEES AND DEFAULT INTEREST
sections.text: If any installment of Base Rent or Additional Rent is not received by Landlord by the 15th day of the month, Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to 10 percent of the overdue installment. Amounts remaining unpaid more than thirty (30) days after the due date shall thereafter bear interest at 9 percent per annum. The late charge and default interest are alternative and not cumulative remedies for the same delinquent installment; in no event shall Tenant be charged both for the same period of delay.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — PERCENTAGE RENT
sections.text: In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay 4 percent of Gross Sales in each Lease Year in excess of a breakpoint of $700,000. 'Gross Sales' means all receipts from business conducted at, from, or fulfilled out of the Premises, whether for cash or credit, and expressly includes internet and telephone orders fulfilled from inventory located at the Premises, and expressly excludes: returns and allowances actually credited; sales, excise and similar taxes collected and remitted; transfers of merchandise to other stores of Tenant not made to avoid percentage rent; and receipts from vending machines maintained for employees. Tenant shall deliver a statement of Gross Sales within 30 days after each Lease Year, and Landlord may audit not more than once per Lease Year.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — HOLDOVER
sections.text: If Tenant remains in possession after expiration without Landlord's written consent, the tenancy shall be one at sufferance terminable at will, and Tenant shall pay for each month or portion of a month of holding over an amount equal to 1.25 times the Base Rent last payable, together with all Additional Rent. The parties agree that the harm from a holdover is difficult to estimate and that this amount is a reasonable forecast of that harm and not a penalty.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Insurance
sections.text: The party in possession shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence, naming the other party as an additional insured, and shall furnish a certificate of insurance on request and on each renewal. Each party waives subrogation against the other to the extent of insurance proceeds actually received.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Severability
sections.text: If any provision of this instrument is held invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that provision shall be reformed to the minimum extent necessary to render it enforceable, and if it cannot be so reformed it shall be severed, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Interpretation and Construction Against Drafter
sections.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect construction. The singular includes the plural. This instrument is the product of negotiation between the parties, and no rule of construction requiring interpretation against the drafting party shall apply. Restrictions on the use of land shall nonetheless be construed in favor of the free use of the land.
